results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: Required Prerequisite: Fetch the first search/results page using SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE (validate the page contains real listings, not just navigation).
Required Step: Paginate 1–N results pages using SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE and store each response content for link extraction.
Optional (if results page looks like a thin shell or missing body text) Fallback: Re-fetch the same URL using SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE (enable rendering and increase timeout to capture dynamic content).
Required Step: Extract candidate listing URLs from results content, de-duplicate, then fetch each listing detail page using SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE (use rendering when details are incomplete without it).
Optional (if scraping many listing URLs) Step: Batch URLs via SCRAPE_DO_CREATE_ASYNC_JOB, poll status with SCRAPE_DO_GET_ASYNC_JOB, then read per-URL outputs using SCRAPE_DO_GET_ASYNC_TASK.
Optional (if you need to manage usage before expanding scope) Next Step: Check remaining credits/limits using SCRAPE_DO_GET_ACCOUNT_INFO.
[Required] [Prerequisite]: Identify a usable non-browser zone using BRIGHTDATA_LIST_WEB_UNLOCKER_ZONES (pick an unblocker/web-unlocker style zone; if none returned, resolve access before proceeding).
[Required] [Step]: Retrieve the target page using BRIGHTDATA_WEB_UNLOCKER (set url and zone; start with data_format=markdown for readable text).

[Required] [Next Step]: Verify BRIGHTDATA_WEB_UNLOCKER output quality (data.content non-empty and not just challenge/login/redirect scaffolding; inspect data.headers for x-brd-status-code and x-brd-error-code to catch silent blocks even when HTTP status is 200).
[Optional (if markdown is thin or parsing needs full markup)] [Next Step]: Re-run the same request using BRIGHTDATA_WEB_UNLOCKER (switch to data_format=raw to capture full HTML).

[Optional (if repeated blocks/timeouts persist or batching multiple URLs)] [Fallback]: Run BRIGHTDATA_CRAWL_API (submit URL list, capture snapshot id), then poll BRIGHTDATA_GET_SNAPSHOT_STATUS until complete and only then download via BRIGHTDATA_GET_SNAPSHOT_RESULTS.
known_pitfalls: [SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE] A successful response can still omit main content (e.g., mostly layout); verify content quality and retry with rendering when needed.
[SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE] Rendered fetches can cost more than non-rendered requests; monitor usage to avoid exhausting credits during large runs.
[SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE] Multi-page and multi-listing runs can return very large text blobs; plan to parse responses programmatically rather than inspecting inline.
[BRIGHTDATA_LIST_WEB_UNLOCKER_ZONES] data.zones can be empty or the call can fail with HTTP 401; scraping cannot proceed until permissions/credentials are fixed.
[BRIGHTDATA_WEB_UNLOCKER] Using an invalid/unprovisioned zone often fails with HTTP 400; browser-type zones can yield client_10090 and empty content.
[BRIGHTDATA_WEB_UNLOCKER] HTTP 200 can still indicate failure; check headers for x-brd-status-code signals like 403/406 and x-brd-error-code (e.g., policy/compliance blocks).
[BRIGHTDATA_WEB_UNLOCKER] Proxy/auth or navigation issues may surface as 407 or x-brd-error-code=navigation_timeout with x-brd-status-code=502; retries may still fail without changing approach.
[BRIGHTDATA_GET_SNAPSHOT_RESULTS] Downloading before BRIGHTDATA_GET_SNAPSHOT_STATUS indicates completion can return empty or partial results.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Parse a JSON scrape response from stdin and extract candidate links from markdown-like content fields.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import sys,json,re,urllib.parse as up
obj=json.load(sys.stdin)
allowed_host=obj.get('allowed_host','example.invalid')
for r in obj.get('results',[]):
 d=r.get('response',{}).get('data',{})
 c=d.get('content','')
 links=[u for u in re.findall(r'\[[^\]]+\]\((https?://[^)]+)\)',c)]
 out=[u for u in links if up.urlparse(u).netloc.endswith(allowed_host)]
 print(out[:50])
```

SCRAPE_DO_GET_PAGE.description: A tool to scrape web pages using scrape.do's API service. Makes a basic GET request to fetch webpage content while handling anti-bot protections and proxy rotation automatically. Does not execute JavaScript by default — pages requiring client-side rendering (SPAs, dynamically loaded content) will return incomplete HTML; use SCRAPE_DO_GET_RENDER_PAGE or set render=true for those cases.

url.description: Target web page URL to scrape

render.description: Enable headless browser rendering Use for JS-heavy pages, SPAs, or sites with anti-bot JS challenges. Increase `timeout` when enabling to ensure full page load before cutoff.

geo_code.description: Choose country for target web page (e.g. 'us', 'gb')

return_json.description: Return network requests in JSON format

set_cookies.description: Set cookies for target web page

BRIGHTDATA_LIST_WEB_UNLOCKER_ZONES.description: Tool to list your configured Web Unlocker zones and proxy endpoints. Use to view available zones for web scraping and bot protection bypass.

BRIGHTDATA_WEB_UNLOCKER.description: Tool to bypass bot detection, captcha, and other anti-scraping measures to extract content from websites. Use when you need to scrape websites that block automated access or require JavaScript rendering. Some responses may still contain CAPTCHA challenge pages or incomplete HTML; inspect the response before retrying, and avoid aggressive retry loops.

url.description: The URL of the website to unlock and scrape.

zone.description: Web Unlocker zone name (required, non-empty). Call BRIGHTDATA_LIST_WEB_UNLOCKER_ZONES first to get available zones.

format.description: Response format - 'raw' returns HTML content as string, 'json' returns structured data.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the proxy location (e.g., 'us', 'gb', 'de').

data_format.description: Set to 'markdown' to convert page content to markdown format.
